questions.stem: Fifty traders in Ariaria market each pay N20,000 a year into a fund from which any member whose shop burns down is compensated. This arrangement illustrates insurance as a scheme in which
options: the government pays for all the losses suffered by its citizens through taxes
a trader avoids paying taxes on his profit
the losses of a few are shared among the many who contribute to a common fund
a bank lends money to customers at low interest
people save money for their children's education only
questions.explanation: Insurance pools contributions so the many pay for the losses of the few.

questions.stem: The person or company that buys an insurance policy is the
questions.explanation: The insured (policyholder) buys cover.

questions.stem: Which of these risks is generally NOT insurable?
options: Fire damage to a warehouse full of imported spare parts and tyres in Nnewi
Theft of stock from a shop
Injury to a worker at the factory
Damage to a car in an accident
A loss from a fall in the price of shares bought for speculation
questions.explanation: Speculative risks, with a chance of gain, are not insurable.

questions.stem: Pure risk differs from speculative risk because pure risk
options: offers a chance of profit for the person as well as a loss
offers only the possibility of loss or no loss
questions.explanation: Pure risks involve loss or no loss; speculative risks can produce gain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of insurance to the national economy?
options: Insurance removes all risks from society
Insurance guarantees a profit for every business that buys a policy
Insurance companies mobilise premiums for long-term investment
Insurance prevents all accidents from happening
questions.explanation: Insurers invest premiums, providing capital for development.

questions.stem: The basic principles of insurance are meant to
options: fix the salaries of insurance staff
guide the formation and operation of insurance contracts
decide the location of insurance offices in each state of the country
determine which bank an insurer uses
set the prices of goods in the market
questions.explanation: Principles such as utmost good faith and indemnity govern insurance contracts.

questions.stem: A person is said to have an insurable interest in a property when he
options: must be a registered member of the insurer's staff or board of directors
must live near the insurance office
must have made a claim before
stands to suffer financial loss if the insured item is lost or damaged
must own shares in the insurer
questions.explanation: Insurable interest is a financial interest in the subject matter.

questions.stem: Which person has an insurable interest in a building?
options: A bank that holds the building as security for a loan
A passer-by who admires the building
A tenant who rents a different building on the next street
A newspaper reporter writing about it
A student who once visited it
questions.explanation: A mortgagee would lose financially if the property were destroyed.

questions.stem: For a policy on goods shipped from Apapa to Abidjan, at what point must the cargo owner have an insurable interest in the goods?
options: only at the time the proposal form is completed
only when the policy is renewed
at the time the ship is built
only when the premium is paid
questions.explanation: Marine insurance requires interest at the time of loss.

questions.stem: The Latin term for the principle of utmost good faith is
questions.explanation: Uberrimae fidei means utmost good faith.

questions.stem: A proposer who fails to disclose that his shop was burgled twice in the past year breaches the principle of
questions.explanation: All material facts must be disclosed.

questions.stem: Which description fits a fact that a proposer is legally bound to disclose to an insurer?
options: is printed in bold on the policy
relates only to the colour of the property and the brand of paint used on its walls
would influence the insurer in accepting the risk or fixing the premium
is known only to the broker
has no effect on the risk
questions.explanation: Material facts affect the underwriter's judgement.

questions.stem: The principle that the insurer pays only if the loss was caused by the dominant, effective cause covered by the policy is
questions.explanation: Proximate cause identifies the active, efficient cause of the loss.

questions.stem: A storm (insured) blew down a wall, and the next day thieves (theft not insured) entered through the gap and stole goods. Applying proximate cause, the theft loss is
options: covered, because the storm made the theft possible by breaking the wall
covered only if the police are informed
not covered, because theft is a new independent cause
covered because the policy is in force
questions.explanation: A new and independent intervening cause breaks the chain.

questions.stem: Settling a fire claim, an insurer pays exactly what it costs to put the shop back to its pre-fire condition. The insurer is applying the idea that insurance should
options: restore the insured to the same financial position as before the loss
make the insured noticeably richer after a loss than he was before the event happened
punish the person who caused the loss
pay the insured double the value of the loss
questions.explanation: Indemnity prevents profit from insurance.

questions.stem: Which type of insurance is NOT a contract of indemnity?
questions.explanation: Human life cannot be valued, so life assurance pays an agreed sum.

questions.stem: A building worth N20 million is insured for N15 million and suffers a loss of N8 million. If the policy is subject to average, the insurer will pay
After paying a claim, an insurer takes over the insured's right to recover the loss from a negligent third party. This is
questions.explanation: Subrogation transfers recovery rights to the insurer.

questions.stem: A car insured comprehensively is damaged by a careless driver. The insurer pays the owner N900,000 and recovers N900,000 from the careless driver's insurer. This recovery is possible because of
questions.explanation: Subrogation lets the insurer step into the insured's shoes.

questions.stem: Contribution applies when
options: the insured has paid his premiums later than the due date
the same risk is insured with two or more insurers
the policy covers life assurance only
the insured makes a fraudulent claim
the loss is caused by an act of war
questions.explanation: Insurers share the loss rateably when there is double insurance.

questions.stem: Property is insured with Insurer A for N3 million and Insurer B for N1 million. A loss of N800,000 occurs. Under contribution by sum insured, Insurer A pays
The documents used in arranging an insurance contract include all of the following EXCEPT the
questions.explanation: A bill of exchange is a payment instrument, not an insurance document.

questions.stem: The form completed by a person seeking insurance, giving details of the risk, is the
questions.explanation: The proposal form is the basis of the contract.

questions.stem: Why does an insurer insist that the proposer signs the statement at the foot of the completed application?
options: makes the answers the basis of the contract
transfers ownership of the property to the insurance company
guarantees that a claim will be paid
questions.explanation: The declaration confirms the truth of answers which form the basis of the contract.

questions.stem: A temporary document giving cover while the policy is being prepared is the
questions.explanation: Cover notes provide interim cover.

questions.stem: A cover note is usually valid for a period of
options: the whole life of the insured person
about 30 days or until the policy is issued
questions.explanation: Cover notes are short-term, commonly up to 30 days.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, a motorist must carry evidence that the vehicle has at least third-party insurance. The document that serves this purpose is the
questions.explanation: The certificate of motor insurance proves compulsory cover.

questions.stem: Which of the following is shown on a motor certificate of insurance?
options: The registration number of the vehicle and the period of cover
The previous claims made by other motorists living in the same state as the insured
The share capital of the insurer
questions.explanation: It identifies the vehicle, insured, persons entitled to drive and period of cover.

questions.stem: Two weeks after paying the premium, Mr Ade receives the full printed contract setting out cover, exclusions and conditions. This document is the
questions.explanation: The policy is the evidence of the contract.

questions.stem: A written alteration attached to a policy to change its terms during its currency is an
questions.explanation: Endorsements change policy terms.

questions.stem: The part of a policy that lists events or losses NOT covered is the
questions.explanation: Exclusions state what is not covered.

questions.stem: Underwriting in insurance practice refers to
options: assessing a risk and deciding whether and on what terms to accept it
paying a claim to the insured
selling cars to members of the public on behalf of insurance companies and brokers
auditing the insurer's accounts at the end of the financial year
questions.explanation: Underwriters evaluate and accept or reject risks.

questions.stem: Re-insurance is the insurance of
options: an insurer's risk by another insurer
questions.explanation: Re-insurance spreads an insurer's large risks.

questions.stem: An insurer passes part of a large risk to a re-insurer. The share kept by the original insurer is called the
questions.explanation: The amount kept is the retention; the amount passed on is ceded.

questions.stem: Which is the main benefit of re-insurance to a direct insurer?
options: It increases the premium paid by the insured on every type of policy
It removes the need for underwriting
It allows the insurer to accept large risks without heavy losses
questions.explanation: Re-insurance spreads large risks and protects capacity.

questions.stem: An insurer sends a policyholder a reminder some weeks before the policy expires. This document is a
questions.explanation: Renewal notices invite the insured to renew.

questions.stem: Days of grace in insurance are
options: days when no claims can be made
days allowed to the proposer to complete, sign and return a proposal form to the insurer
extra days allowed after the renewal date for payment of the premium
days for the insurer to inspect property
questions.explanation: Days of grace allow late payment without lapse, mainly in life assurance.

questions.stem: A request by the insured for payment after a loss is a
questions.explanation: A claim requests compensation.

questions.stem: A professional appointed to investigate and assess the amount of a loss is a
questions.explanation: Loss adjusters investigate and measure claims.

questions.stem: A payment made by an insurer as goodwill even though it is not legally bound to pay under the policy is an
questions.explanation: Ex gratia payments are made voluntarily.

questions.stem: The amount paid by the insured to the insurer for cover is the
questions.explanation: Premium is the price of insurance.

questions.stem: A shop owner insures stock worth N4,000,000 at a rate of 0.75%. The premium payable is
Which of the following is a non-life insurance product?
questions.explanation: Fire insurance is general (non-life) business.

questions.stem: A Keke NAPEP rider who wants only the cheapest cover that keeps him within the law must buy
questions.explanation: Third-party motor insurance is compulsory.

questions.stem: A comprehensive motor policy covers
options: goods carried in a ship belonging to the owner of the insured vehicle
damage to the insured's own vehicle as well as third-party liability
the building where the car is parked overnight by the owner
questions.explanation: Comprehensive cover includes own damage plus third-party liability.

questions.stem: A motorist agrees to bear the first N50,000 of every own-damage claim in return for a lower premium. This N50,000 is the
questions.explanation: The excess is borne by the insured.

questions.stem: A standard fire policy mainly covers loss caused by
questions.explanation: Basic fire cover is fire, lightning and limited explosion.

questions.stem: Additional risks such as storm, flood and riot added to a fire policy for extra premium are called
questions.explanation: Special (allied) perils extend fire cover.

questions.stem: Which of the following would an insurer be most likely to reject under a fire policy?
options: A fire caused by lightning striking the roof during a heavy thunderstorm
An accidental fire from a faulty electrical wire
A fire started by a careless neighbour
A fire spreading from a nearby market
A fire deliberately started by the insured to claim money
questions.explanation: Wilful acts of the insured are not covered.

questions.stem: Burglary insurance normally requires evidence of
options: forcible and violent entry into or exit from the premises
payment of salary to the night guards employed at the premises
questions.explanation: Burglary cover usually needs forcible entry or exit.

questions.stem: Which loss is most likely to be covered under a burglary policy for a shop?
options: Goods stolen secretly by a trusted shop assistant over several months
Goods damaged by rain through a leaking roof
Goods lost through wrong counting by the owner
Goods sold on credit to a customer who refused to pay
Goods stolen after thieves broke the back door at night
questions.explanation: Theft following forcible entry is covered; employee dishonesty needs fidelity cover.

questions.stem: Money insurance is suitable for a business that
options: employs many factory workers on three separate shifts
carries cash between its premises and the bank
questions.explanation: Money insurance covers cash in transit and on premises.

questions.stem: Which is a typical condition of a money insurance policy?
options: The insured must not open a bank account
Cash above a stated limit must be carried with escorts
All cash must be kept outside a safe
The policy covers cash lost through bad debts owed by customers
questions.explanation: Insurers often require escorts and safes for large sums.

questions.stem: A firm buys fidelity guarantee cover. The loss it is protected against is
questions.explanation: Fidelity guarantee covers employee dishonesty.

questions.stem: A cashier steals N2.5 million from his employer over six months. The employer's claim would be paid under
questions.explanation: Employee embezzlement is a fidelity guarantee risk.

questions.stem: Engineering insurance is designed to cover
options: breakdown of machinery and plant such as boilers and lifts
injury to members of the public visiting the premises
questions.explanation: Engineering insurance covers machinery breakdown and related risks.

questions.stem: A contractor building a bridge wants cover against damage to the works during construction. The suitable policy is
questions.explanation: Contractors' all risks covers works under construction.

questions.stem: Marine hull insurance covers
questions.explanation: Hull insurance is on the vessel.

questions.stem: Damage or sacrifice made intentionally to save a ship and its cargo in danger, shared by all interested parties, is
questions.explanation: General average losses are shared by ship and cargo owners.

questions.stem: Cargo is so badly damaged that the cost of saving it would exceed its value, so the owner abandons it to the insurer. This is a
questions.explanation: Constructive total loss occurs where recovery is uneconomic.

questions.stem: Aviation insurance covers
options: aircraft and liabilities arising from their operation
questions.explanation: It covers hull and liabilities of aircraft operators.

questions.stem: Under an aviation policy, the liability of an airline for injury to people on the ground caused by a crashing aircraft is called
questions.explanation: People on the ground are third parties.

questions.stem: Employer's liability insurance covers an employer against
options: loss of profits after a fire
legal liability for injury or disease suffered by employees in the course of work
damage to customers' cars parked within the premises of the business
questions.explanation: It covers liability to employees for work injuries.

questions.stem: A factory worker loses a finger while operating an unguarded machine and sues the company. The company's defence costs and damages would be met by
questions.explanation: Injury to employees at work falls under employer's liability.

questions.stem: A customer slips on a wet floor in a supermarket and is injured. The supermarket's liability is covered by
questions.explanation: Injury to members of the public is a public liability risk.

questions.stem: Public liability insurance would NOT cover
options: injury to visitors on the premises
damage to a neighbour's property caused by the insured's business
injury to the insured's own employees at work
injury to customers from a falling signboard
damage to passers-by's cars from falling objects
questions.explanation: Employees are covered under employer's liability.

questions.stem: Professional indemnity insurance is mainly bought by
questions.explanation: Professionals insure against claims for negligent advice or service.

questions.stem: An architect's faulty design causes a client's building to crack, and the client sues. The architect's suitable cover is
questions.explanation: Negligence in professional services falls under professional indemnity.

questions.stem: Business interruption (consequential loss) insurance covers
options: the cost of rebuilding the premises only, without any other expenses
theft of stock from a locked warehouse by armed robbers at night
loss of profit and extra expenses after an insured damage halts business
questions.explanation: It covers lost profits following insured damage.

questions.stem: Business interruption insurance can normally be bought only when the business also has
options: a life assurance policy covering the owner and his family
a material damage policy such as fire insurance
questions.explanation: BI cover depends on an underlying material damage policy.

questions.stem: Personal accident insurance pays compensation for
options: death or bodily injury caused by an accident
questions.explanation: It pays benefits for accidental injury or death.

questions.stem: Under a personal accident policy, benefits are usually stated as
options: fixed sums for death, loss of limbs and disablement
the market value of the insured's car on the day of the accident
the profits lost by the business
the cost of rebuilding a house
questions.explanation: Benefits are scheduled fixed amounts.

questions.stem: An insurance broker is
options: a person who investigates and assesses claims on behalf of insurers
the owner of the insured property
an independent intermediary who arranges insurance for clients
questions.explanation: Brokers act for the insured.

questions.stem: The person who uses statistics to calculate risks and premium rates, especially in life assurance, is an
questions.explanation: Actuaries apply statistics to insurance.

questions.stem: The professional body for the training and examination of insurance practitioners in Nigeria is the
options: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria
questions.explanation: The CIIN trains and certifies insurance professionals.

questions.stem: The body that regulates insurance business in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: NAICOM supervises and regulates insurance in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the insurance regulator in Nigeria?
options: Selling policies directly to the public
Fixing the prices at which motor vehicles are sold to insured persons
Licensing and supervising insurance companies and intermediaries
questions.explanation: The regulator licenses, supervises and protects policyholders.

questions.stem: The amount that the insurer will pay at most under a policy is the
questions.explanation: The sum insured is the maximum liability.

questions.stem: Damaged property that becomes the insurer's after paying a total loss claim is known as
questions.explanation: Salvage is what remains of damaged property.

questions.stem: An insurer refuses to cover a petrol station unless fire extinguishers are installed and checked monthly. This promise by the insured, on which cover depends, is a
questions.explanation: A warranty is a condition the insured promises to observe; breach can void cover.

questions.stem:
Case study: Mrs Oyibo owns a provision store in Asaba valued at N12,000,000. She insured the stock against fire with Alpha Insurance for N6,000,000 and with Beta Insurance for N3,000,000. When completing the proposal forms, she did not mention that a fire had damaged her previous shop two years earlier. Last month an electrical fault in a neighbouring shop, owned by Mr Emeka, spread fire into her store and destroyed stock worth N4,000,000. The fire service report confirmed that Mr Emeka had used illegal wiring.
(a) Identify the principle of insurance that Mrs Oyibo breached and explain its possible effect on her claim. [5 marks]
(b) Explain how the principle of contribution would apply if the claim were valid, and calculate the share of each insurer, ignoring average. [6 marks]
(c) Explain how subrogation could be used by the insurers after paying the claim. [5 marks]
(d) State two ways Mrs Oyibo could have improved her insurance arrangement. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei)
3 marks: non-disclosure of a material fact (previous fire) may allow the insurers to avoid the policy or refuse the claim
2 marks: with double insurance, insurers share the loss rateably so the insured is not over-compensated
2 marks: Alpha pays 6/9 x 4,000,000 = N2,666,667
2 marks: Beta pays 3/9 x 4,000,000 = N1,333,333
2 marks: after paying, insurers take over Mrs Oyibo's rights against the negligent party
3 marks: they may sue Mr Emeka (or his liability insurer) to recover the amount paid, up to the amount paid
2 marks: disclose all material facts fully
2 marks: insure for the full value of the stock to avoid underinsurance / add business interruption cover
questions.explanation: Failure to disclose the earlier fire breaches utmost good faith and may make the policies voidable. If valid, contribution shares the N4,000,000 loss in proportion to sums insured: Alpha 6/9 = N2,666,667 and Beta 3/9 = N1,333,333. Through subrogation the insurers may recover from Mr Emeka, whose illegal wiring caused the fire. She should disclose fully and insure for full value (under the average condition, being under-insured could reduce payment).

questions.stem:
(a) Define insurance. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four functions of insurance. [8 marks]
(c) Distinguish between pure risk and speculative risk, giving one example of each. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: a contract in which the insurer, for a premium, agrees to compensate the insured for loss from specified risks, so that the losses of a few are shared by many
2 marks: provides financial protection/security against loss
2 marks: spreads risk across many policyholders
2 marks: encourages investment and business enterprise
2 marks: mobilises funds for national development / promotes loss prevention / serves as collateral for loans
1 mark: pure risk: only loss or no loss
1 mark: example: fire, theft, accident
1 mark: speculative risk: possibility of gain or loss
1 mark: example: gambling, share trading, starting a business
questions.explanation: Insurance is a contract where a premium buys a promise of compensation for specified losses, pooling risks so the many pay for the few. It provides security, spreads risk, encourages enterprise, mobilises investment funds, supports credit and promotes loss prevention. Pure risks (fire, theft) give loss or no loss and are insurable; speculative risks (shares, gambling) may give gain and are not.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the principle of insurable interest. [3 marks]
(b) State three essentials of insurable interest. [6 marks]
(c) Give three examples of persons who have insurable interest in property they do not fully own. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: the insured must stand to lose financially if the subject matter is lost or damaged, and to benefit from its safety
2 marks: there must be property, life, rights or liability capable of being insured
2 marks: the insured must have a legally recognised relationship with the subject matter
2 marks: the insured must suffer financial loss from the event
2 marks: a mortgagee (bank) holding property as security
2 marks: a bailee such as a dry cleaner or warehouse keeper holding customers' goods
2 marks: a tenant liable for repairs / a hirer under hire purchase / a part-owner
questions.explanation: Insurable interest is a legally recognised financial interest in the subject matter. It requires property or liability capable of insurance, a legal relationship with it, and financial loss if it is damaged. Mortgagees, bailees, tenants with repair obligations, hire-purchase hirers and joint owners all have insurable interest.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the principle of indemnity. [3 marks]
(b) State three methods by which an insurer may provide indemnity. [6 marks]
(c) A warehouse worth N50,000,000 is insured for N40,000,000 under a policy subject to average. A fire causes damage of N15,000,000. Calculate the amount payable and explain why the insured does not receive the full loss. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: the insured is restored to the same financial position as just before the loss, with no profit from the claim
2 marks: cash payment
2 marks: repair of the damaged property
2 marks: replacement or reinstatement
2 marks: formula: sum insured / value x loss
2 marks: 40/50 x 15,000,000 = N12,000,000
2 marks: the property was underinsured, so the insured bears a proportion of the loss himself
questions.explanation: Indemnity restores the insured to the pre-loss financial position. Insurers indemnify by cash, repair, replacement or reinstatement. Under average, payment = 40,000,000 / 50,000,000 x 15,000,000 = N12,000,000; the insured, being underinsured by one-fifth, bears N3,000,000 himself.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a proposal form? [3 marks]
(b) State four items of information contained in a motor insurance proposal form. [4 marks]
(c) Distinguish between a cover note and a policy. [4 marks]
(d) State two uses of a certificate of insurance. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: a form completed by a proposer giving full details of the risk, on which the insurer decides whether and on what terms to accept it
1 mark: name, address and occupation of the proposer
1 mark: make, model and registration number of the vehicle
1 mark: use of the vehicle and value
1 mark: driving experience / previous accidents and claims / type of cover required
2 marks: a cover note is a temporary document giving interim cover
2 marks: a policy is the formal and full evidence of the contract, with all terms and conditions
2 marks: it is legal evidence that compulsory insurance (e.g. motor third-party) exists
2 marks: it can be shown to police/authorities and identifies the vehicle, insured and period of cover
questions.explanation: A proposal form is the application giving material facts about the risk. A motor proposal asks for the proposer's details, vehicle make/model/registration, use, value, driving history and cover required. A cover note gives temporary cover; the policy is the full contract. The certificate proves compulsory insurance to the police and identifies the vehicle and period.

questions.stem:
(a) What is re-insurance? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four reasons why insurance companies re-insure. [8 marks]
(c) Distinguish between facultative and treaty re-insurance. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: the transfer by an insurer of part of the risks it has accepted to another insurer (re-insurer) for a premium
2 marks: to spread large risks and avoid catastrophic loss
2 marks: to increase underwriting capacity to accept large risks
2 marks: to stabilise results / profits from year to year
2 marks: to benefit from the technical expertise of re-insurers / meet regulatory requirements
2 marks: facultative: each risk offered and accepted individually; the re-insurer may accept or decline
2 marks: treaty: an agreement covering a class of risks automatically within agreed limits
questions.explanation: Re-insurance is insurance for insurers. Insurers re-insure to spread large risks, increase capacity, stabilise results, protect solvency and gain expertise. Facultative re-insurance is negotiated risk by risk; treaty re-insurance covers agreed classes automatically.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain three types of motor insurance policies. [9 marks]
(b) State three procedures a motorist should follow when his insured car is involved in an accident. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: third-party only: covers liability for death, injury or property damage to third parties (compulsory)
3 marks: third-party, fire and theft: third-party cover plus loss of the insured vehicle by fire or theft
3 marks: comprehensive: third-party cover plus accidental damage to the insured's own vehicle and other benefits
2 marks: report the accident to the police and obtain a police report
2 marks: notify the insurer promptly and complete a claim form
2 marks: obtain details of witnesses/other parties, take photographs, obtain repair estimates and not admit liability
questions.explanation: Motor policies are third-party only (compulsory), third-party fire and theft, and comprehensive. After an accident, report to the police, inform the insurer quickly and complete the claim form, collect details and evidence, obtain estimates and avoid admitting liability.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between marine hull insurance and marine cargo insurance. [4 marks]
(b) Explain the following terms: (i) general average; (ii) particular average; (iii) actual total loss. [9 marks]
(c) State one difference between a voyage policy and a time policy. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: hull insurance covers the ship and its machinery
2 marks: cargo insurance covers goods carried by the ship
3 marks: general average: intentional sacrifice or expense to save the common adventure, shared by all parties
3 marks: particular average: partial accidental loss borne by the owner of the damaged interest alone
3 marks: actual total loss: the subject matter is destroyed or irretrievably lost
2 marks: a voyage policy covers a particular journey; a time policy covers a fixed period
questions.explanation: Hull insurance covers the vessel; cargo insurance covers goods. General average is a deliberate sacrifice for the common safety, shared rateably; particular average is a partial accidental loss falling on one interest; actual total loss is complete destruction or irrecoverable loss. Voyage policies cover a journey, time policies a period.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four operators in the Nigerian insurance market. [4 marks]
(b) Explain the role of each of the following: (i) insurance broker; (ii) insurance agent; (iii) loss adjuster. [9 marks]
(c) Name the professional body of insurance brokers in Nigeria. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: insurance companies (insurers)
1 mark: re-insurance companies
1 mark: insurance brokers
1 mark: agents / loss adjusters / actuaries
3 marks: broker: independent professional who advises the insured and places cover with suitable insurers
3 marks: agent: represents an insurer to sell its policies and collect premiums for commission
3 marks: loss adjuster: investigates and assesses claims impartially and recommends settlement
2 marks: Nigerian Council of Registered Insurance Brokers (NCRIB)
questions.explanation: Operators include insurers, re-insurers, brokers, agents, loss adjusters and actuaries. Brokers advise clients and place cover; agents sell for an insurer for commission; loss adjusters investigate and assess claims. Brokers belong to the Nigerian Council of Registered Insurance Brokers.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the body that regulates insurance business in Nigeria. [2 marks]
(b) Explain five functions of the insurance regulator in Nigeria. [10 marks]
(c) State three ways insurance regulation protects policyholders. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: National Insurance Commission (NAICOM)
2 marks: registering and licensing insurers and intermediaries
2 marks: supervising and inspecting insurance companies
2 marks: setting standards, minimum capital and solvency requirements
2 marks: approving rates/policy wordings and protecting policyholders' interests
2 marks: settling complaints and disputes / advising government on insurance
1 mark: ensures insurers are solvent and can pay claims
1 mark: handles complaints against insurers
1 mark: prevents fraudulent or unfair practices
questions.explanation: NAICOM regulates insurance in Nigeria. It licenses insurers and intermediaries, supervises and inspects them, sets capital and solvency standards, approves products, resolves complaints and advises government. This keeps insurers solvent, gives policyholders a complaints channel and curbs unfair practices.
